gaps.sentence: By Friday, the climbers ___ on the north face for six days without a break.
gaps.hint: duration measured to a future point
gaps.explanation: 'By Friday + for six days' calls for the future perfect: will have been.

gaps.sentence: She ___ two majors when she was at university.
gaps.hint: a completed period in the past
gaps.explanation: A completed past period takes the past simple: did.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her keys again — this is the third time this month!
gaps.hint: third time this month connects to now
gaps.explanation: 'This is the third time' links a recent event to now, so the present perfect is required: has lost.

gaps.sentence: By the time you read this letter, I ___ the country.
gaps.explanation: An action completed before a future point takes the future perfect: will have left.

gaps.sentence: Every morning she ___ an hour in the garden before breakfast.
gaps.explanation: 'Every morning' marks a repeated routine, which takes the present simple: spends.

gaps.sentence: He rarely ___ his laptop on Sundays because he prefers to rest.
gaps.explanation: Frequency adverbs such as 'rarely' mark habitual actions, which take the present simple: uses.

gaps.sentence: The moon ___ round the Earth roughly every 27 days.
gaps.hint: a timeless fact about the moon
gaps.explanation: Timeless facts take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: My back hurts because I ___ the garden all afternoon.
gaps.hint: all afternoon explains the present pain
gaps.explanation: A recent continuous activity with a visible present result takes the present perfect continuous: have been digging.
